headline: Calmer warnings while you ride

items.title: Warning lights
items.line: Small icons at the top of the ride screen, like a car's dashboard: red, amber or blue, and nothing when all is fine. At a stop, tap one to read it.

items.title: Battery turns amber, then red
items.line: The battery number and its edge turn amber at 20 % and red at 10 %.

items.title: Turn back in two steps
items.line: On a tight trip you hear "Turn-back point in one kilometre", then "Turn back now to make it back" at the point.

full: Less urgent warnings play one soft tone instead of speaking.
Fast speeds are always kept: a reading above 50 km/h, or a sudden jump, is no longer thrown away.

headline: The app comes alive

items.title: Your scooter on the Lock Screen
items.line: When the scooter connects, a card shows km left with a Start ride button. While riding it quietly shows Recording, and at your destination End ride or Keep going.

items.title: Your ride draws itself
items.line: After a ride, and the first time you open one, the route draws in its speed colours with a sound and a buzz you can feel that follows your speed.

items.title: Start from Control Center
items.line: Add Free ride or Ride to next to Control Center or the Action button, or ask Siri: "Ride to Work in CorckieApp".

items.title: Touch the charts
items.line: Drag across Stats bars or the Battery log to read each day or moment.

full: On iOS 26 the tab bar, map buttons and live tiles are Liquid Glass. Sunlight mode keeps solid panels.
Cards grow into their screens and shrink back when you swipe down (iOS 18).
Icons react: Start squishes, the bag hops when you pick a load, the charging bolt pulses, the gear turns.
While charging, the Battery card glows softly; it turns green-gold when full.
New sounds for connecting, starting, ending, plugging in, a full charge and saving. Settings → Sounds → Charging and saving turns the new ones off.
One clear rule for vibration, and Settings → Sounds → Vibration turns it all off.
Ride, route and place lists shrink a little at the edges as you scroll.

headline: Calmer screens, safer backups

items.title: A clearer Battery log
items.line: One smooth battery line with your average, Day and Week views, and a single line on top: % now, charges and rides. Tap a day to open it.

items.title: Backups off the phone
items.line: Settings → Data & backup → Backup: choose a folder in iCloud Drive and every ride is backed up there. If the folder is gone, backups stay on the phone until you choose it again.

items.title: Remove a place
items.line: Open a place and tap Remove place. It leaves Where to, Home and the maps; past rides keep its name. Places → Removed places puts it back.

full: The ⓘ explanations open right under their heading instead of a sheet; tap again to close.
The tab you're on shows its name.
Lists fade softly above the tab bar, and a light blur sits behind the tab bar and the map buttons.
Restoring rider info from an older backup works after this update too.

headline: More control, fewer surprises

items.title: Every alert has its own switch
items.line: Settings → Notifications lists them in groups: rides, charging and tips. Switch-on, charge and battery wear alerts can now be turned off one by one.

items.title: Your own charging speed
items.line: Battery → Measure charging speed: type the scooter's % every 20 minutes while it charges, and the charge-time estimates use your speed.

items.title: Bring your rides back
items.line: After Start fresh without keeping your info, Bring rider info back returns your places, routes and old rides. Setup also has a Restore link for a new phone.

full: Prices are one screen: fuel price, electricity and fuel use, and price history.
Settings → Battery is now called Battery setup, so it no longer shares a name with the Battery page.
The battery size is learned from your rides (for example 16 Ah, learned from 5 rides) and the pack voltage class is noted.
Home says when iPhone notifications are off, and a ride says when Motion is off, each with a way to Settings.
A ride with no GPS says why and how to fix it.
Tyre pressure no longer shows a fixed number; check it against your scooter's manual.

headline: Welcome to CorckieApp

items.title: Ready for a new scooter
items.line: Settings → Data & backup → Start fresh makes a backup, then starts the battery numbers over. Setup now shows which scooter it found (model, km, battery) before you connect.

items.title: Bluetooth, explained
items.line: If Bluetooth is off or not allowed for CorckieApp, Home and setup say so and take you to the right place.

items.title: A cleaner app
items.line: Test buttons and notes are gone from your screens, and the build is ready for other riders.

full: Start fresh (Settings → Data & backup): a backup first, then the scooter's battery numbers and estimates start over. You choose whether your places, routes and ride times stay.
Setup names the scooter it found (for example “RND G100 · 3 km · 87 %”), so you can match the km with its dashboard. The scooter is saved only when you press Connect, and the closest one is chosen.
A clear message when Bluetooth is off or not allowed for CorckieApp, on Home and in setup.
The iPhone's Bluetooth question is explained on the first setup screen.
Thumbs and notes on rides are gone.
A copy of your data is made before an update, and the update-failed screen says how to share the report.
A clearer message when your data comes from a newer version of the app.
